title: Linux Networking & Isolation
subtitle: Kernel primitives that isolate, connect and route workloads.

tiles.label: Network namespaces
tiles.says: Linux manages namespaces so each workload owns a network stack.
tiles.detail: Separate interfaces, routes and firewall rules give clean isolation on one host.

tiles.label: Cgroups
tiles.says: Linux manages cgroups to cap CPU, memory and I/O.
tiles.detail: Resource limits keep neighbours from interfering and make capacity predictable.

tiles.label: Mount namespaces
tiles.says: Linux manages mounts so each process sees its own filesystem.
tiles.detail: Private mount views underpin containers and sandboxing.

tiles.label: veth pairs
tiles.says: veth pairs are virtual cables between namespaces.
tiles.detail: One end in the namespace, one on the host, carrying frames both ways.

tiles.label: Bridges
tiles.says: A bridge acts as a virtual layer 2 switch.
tiles.detail: It joins veth ends into one subnet using MAC learning.

tiles.label: VLANs & bonds
tiles.says: VLANs and bonds segment and aggregate links.
tiles.detail: Tagged traffic and link redundancy bring switch-like features to servers.

tiles.label: IP forwarding
tiles.says: ip_forward turns a host into a router.
tiles.detail: The routing table sends packets between interfaces and subnets.

tiles.label: iptables & nftables
tiles.detail: MASQUERADE and DNAT share addresses and publish services, and filters enforce policy.

tiles.label: keepalived VRRP
tiles.says: VRRP floats a virtual address between hosts.
tiles.detail: Failover happens in seconds, so a gateway or load balancer survives host loss.

declarations: Everything on Linux is a file or a namespace.
Bridge connects; routes forward; NAT translates.
Limit with cgroups, isolate with namespaces.
